comment: Subject id vectors, consumed by both the PHP and the TypeScript suite so the two id grammars are asserted equal rather than assumed so. "valid" and "invalid" are the context-free grammar, which both implementations answer alike. "canonicalization" needs the local Source key and so is the PHP parser's alone. See docs/reference/subject-format.md.

valid.case: a bare local id stays bare
the full local alphabet is accepted
another wiki's Subject keeps its qualified form
a foreign localId follows its own grammar, not the local one
a foreign localId may be numeric
only the first colon separates, so a localId may contain colons
a Source key may hold digits, hyphens and underscores after the first letter
a Source key of the maximum length
a localId of the maximum length

invalid.case: empty
a bare id that is not a local id
a bare id one character too short
a bare id one character too long
a bare id using an omitted alphabet character
a bare id with a trailing newline
a qualified id with a trailing newline
a Source key holding a newline
an empty Source key
an empty localId
a Source key starting with a digit
a Source key holding a dot
a Source key over 64 characters
a localId over 256 characters
a localId holding a path separator
a localId holding a query separator
a localId holding a fragment separator
a localId holding a percent sign
a localId holding a space
a localId holding a tab
a localId holding a newline
a localId holding a control character
a localId holding an ampersand
a localId holding an apostrophe
a localId holding a quotation mark
a localId holding an angle bracket
a localId holding a backslash
a localId holding a square bracket
a localId holding a curly brace
a localId holding a non-ASCII character

canonicalization.comment: Ids that only mean something once the local Source key is known. Canonicalization happens on the write path, which is PHP; the frontend only ever sees ids already in canonical form, so the TypeScript suite skips these.

valid.case: an id qualified with the local key canonicalizes to bare

invalid.case: the local key with a localId the local grammar rejects
the local key with a localId holding a colon, which is not the local grammar
the local key applied twice
